description: Knowledge body for Stage 2 rules layer. Pair, triadic, and feeling-block cross-reference entries assembled via Perplexity RAG (Claude 4.5 Sonnet thinking mode) with BoardGameGeek exemplar verification inline during generation. Pre-workshop grounding. To be refined post-weekend field notes.
assembly_source: Perplexity reasoning mode × 6 clustered calls (24 April 2026). Each call produced 10-15 entries with BGG-verified exemplars. Remaining gaps filled post-workshop.

verification_status_definitions.perplexity-bgg-verified: Exemplars cited with BGG ID or tag reference in generation; considered production-ready pending workshop field notes
verification_status_definitions.perplexity-flagged-check: Exemplar named without BGG ID — spot-check recommended before workshop use
verification_status_definitions.pending-audit: Not yet spot-checked against live BGG data

pairs.tendency: Players keep risking more to grab rewards while trying to knock others back, creating exciting back-and-forth chases.
pros: Adds surprise attacks that keep everyone guessing next moves.
Makes turns feel tense and full of big swings in who leads.
cons: One bad risk can let someone else pull way ahead suddenly.
Lots of player hits might slow down the fun flow.

pairs.tendency: The group decides together when to push for bigger team wins against a shared challenge, like betting on a group dare.
pros: Builds teamwork as everyone cheers on shared risks.
Heightens group thrill when bold moves pay off for all.
cons: A single failed push can hurt the whole team's progress.
Group debates over risks might take extra time.

exemplars_removed.reason: BoardGameGeek tags: Cooperative, Deduction, Trick-taking; no push your luck

pairs.tendency: People place helpers to claim spots but bump others off or fight for key areas, like competing for the best playground swings.
pros: Turns blocking into smart ways to shape the game board.
Keeps choices connected since your spot affects friends' plans.
cons: Popular spots fill fast, leaving fewer good options later.
Direct bumps can make early turns feel crowded and frustrating.

pairs.tendency: You place your workers on a board next to pretend opponents or alone, racing your own goals like building your dream town quietly.
pros: Lets you focus on personal plans without waiting for others.
Feels like a private challenge you control at your pace.
cons: Less chatting with friends since paths don't cross much.
Auto-opponents might block spots in repeating ways.

pairs.tendency: Friends pick from shared options then use them to mess with each other's setups, like choosing cards to prank rivals.
pros: Picking sharpens what you take to target others cleverly.
Creates lively rivalries over who grabs the best counter-picks.
cons: Strong early picks widen gaps between leaders and catch-ups.
Targets feel personal and might upset balanced play.

exemplars_removed.reason: BoardGameGeek full tags (https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/63888): drafting absent

pairs.tendency: Everyone passes choices around to build a team plan against the game, like sharing puzzle pieces for a group picture.
pros: Sharing picks helps the team cover all needs together.
Encourages talk about who takes what for best group fit.
cons: Uneven picks might leave weak spots no one covers.
Passing loops can feel slow if talks drag on.

exemplars_removed.reason: BoardGameGeek: Tile Placement, Memory, Pattern Recognition; competitive, most points wins
BoardGameGeek: Open Drafting, Race; competitive, one champion

pairs.tendency: Groups battle to claim and hold map spots by pushing out rivals, like teams claiming neighborhood forts.
pros: Sparks fierce fights over valuable lands that matter most.
Rewards bold moves to flip control in key battles.
cons: Losing battles wipes out hard-earned progress quickly.
Maps get chaotic with constant back-and-forth fights.

pairs.tendency: Players grow strength on the board to nudge out others without head-on clashes, like plants overtaking a garden patch.
pros: Lets clever positioning shift power without mean attacks.
Board state guides natural rivalries over time.
cons: Slow builds mean late-game surprises from quiet leaders.
Ties in areas create uncertainty on who gains what.

pairs.tendency: The team follows suit rules to hit shared trick goals against the deck, like passing secret signals in a group quest.
pros: Suit following builds trust in team card plays.
Shared missions make every trick a team story moment.
cons: One wrong lead can derail the whole mission chain.
Strict rules limit wild plays for comebacks.
exemplars: The Crew: The Quest for Planet Nine

exemplars_removed.reason: BoardGameGeek full tags (https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/373106): trick-taking absent

pairs.tendency: Partners signal quietly during tricks to outscore the other pair, like spouses guessing each other's card hints.
pros: Partner signals add hidden teamwork layers.
Team wins feel shared without solo pressure.
cons: Misread signals lead to big team losses unexpectedly.
Uneven partners create blame during tough hands.

pairs.tendency: You roll dice to move your piece along a path, and it feels like a fun dash where luck decides who dashes ahead first.
pros: Quick and easy to play for everyone.
Exciting surprises from dice rolls keep it lively.
cons: Little choice means smart plans don't matter much.
One bad roll can end your lead fast.

pairs.tendency: You pick cards from a shared pool to build your score, feeling like a clever trade where choices shape your total.
cons: Bad picks early hurt your whole game.

pairs.tendency: You place workers on spots to grab resources and build points, feeling like careful planning to grow your score biggest.
cons: Running out of spots frustrates waits.

pairs.tendency: You gather matching items like colors or types for points, feeling like hunting treasures to complete fun groups.
cons: Too many same items waste space.

pairs.tendency: You lay tiles to build areas and score, feeling like growing a pretty map where connections boost your points.
You claim map spots to push others out, feeling like a battle where you fight to stay in till the end.
cons: Can feel mean to new players.

exemplars_removed.reason: BoardGameGeek full tags (https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/170216): last-standing absent

pairs.tendency: You risk more draws or rolls for rewards, feeling like a dare where luck decides if you win big or bust.
You place workers with tiny luck, feeling like a brainy puzzle where smart spots win the day.
You draft with some luck but choices tame it, feeling like smart picks turn chance into wins.
You play cards from hand amid draws but discard to fix bad luck, feeling like steering fate with your choices.
Players work as a team but can't freely talk about their secret cards, so they give hints to share info without saying it straight.
pros: Builds fun puzzle-solving as a group.
Makes teamwork feel clever and tricky.
cons: Wrong guesses lead to quick losses.
pairs.tension_note: Creates a communication constraint where team trust relies on subtle clues instead of open chat. This IS the game.

pairs.tendency: Everyone sees all cards and plans openly, focusing on smart group choices against the game.
pros: Easy talk leads to strong plans.
Feels like true teamwork with no secrets.
cons: Can feel like arguing over moves (alpha-player problem).

pairs.tendency: A secret betrayer hides among the group, pretending to help while sabotaging quietly.
Players attack each other face-to-face while lying about their strength or plans to fool foes.
Players clash openly but hide their cards, guessing enemy power during fights.

exemplars_removed.reason: power cards are kept face up (rulebook); no hidden hands

pairs.tendency: Rival teams battle, but secret roles within teams create internal doubt and spies.
The team fights to stay alive together against tough threats like zombies or disasters.
Players unite on one big goal, like curing diseases or building a wonder.
Players bash each other until only one monster or warrior remains victorious.
pros: Simple fights are fast and fun.

pairs.tendency: Players mostly cooperate but chase personal goals, with a traitor undermining all.
Players feel sneaky excitement guessing what others hold while carefully timing their own card plays.
pros: Rewards smart card timing over luck.
cons: Can frustrate if hands get stuck.

pairs.tendency: Everyone sees all cards, so turns feel like a public puzzle where order of play creates clever chains.
pros: Fair competition with no hidden surprises.
Easy to teach strategy through visible choices.

destination tickets are secret; not full information

pairs.tendency: Bidding blindly on secret values sparks wild guesses and laughs from overpaying surprises.
pros: Quick rounds with high bluff potential.
cons: Feels unfair if luck swings bids.
Hard for kids to gauge hidden worth.

pairs.tendency: Open bids on known items turn into tense number-crunching standoffs over exact worth.

pairs.tendency: Tricks reveal clues bit by bit, making each lead a thrilling aha moment or swing of suspicion.
pros: Short games build deduction skills fast.
cons: Frustrates if one player deduces early.

pairs.tendency: Placing workers uncovers shared secrets, turning the board into a detective map of motives.

exemplars_removed.reason: BoardGameGeek: Area Movement, Dice Rolling, Hand Management; no worker placement
BoardGameGeek: Hand Management only

pairs.tendency: Risky presses with fake bravado create hilarious busts or epic steals from the pot.

pairs.tendency: Fake bids bait opponents into costly folds, making auctions a theater of fake confidence.

pairs.tendency: Secret sets build surprise reveals, but trades force tough reveals of partial hands.
cons: Dead hands stall if no trades.

pairs.tendency: Open board invites rivalry over spots, where every tile locks in chain reactions everyone sees.
Players sneak toward secret wins while hiding their cards, making everyone suspicious of each other.
pros: Builds tension through bluffing and mind-reading.
Encourages clever card plays opponents can't predict.
cons: Can lead to arguments over suspected cheating.
Harder for new players to grasp hidden strategies.

pairs.tendency: Secret goals create surprise twists even when the board shows everything else clearly.
pros: Board transparency lets players focus on strategy.
Opponents can guess goals from public actions.
cons: Guessing goals might frustrate if too obvious or too hidden.
Full view can make blocking easy once goals are spotted.

exemplars_removed.reason: Days of Wonder rulebook: players keep their Destination Tickets secret until the end of the game; not full information

pairs.tendency: Teammates hide cards to fight shared threats, but must share info carefully to survive together.
pros: Prevents alpha gaming where one player bosses everyone.
Forces real teamwork through trading and requests.
cons: Poor communication leads to failed plans easily.
Hand limits create tough choices on what to share.

pairs.tendency: Everyone sees the scores and plans, turning it into a fair race to build the biggest total.
pros: Easy to balance strategies since all moves are visible.
cons: Leader gets ganged up on, feeling unfair late game.
Can turn cutthroat as players block obvious point grabs.

pairs.tendency: Perfect setup for brainy showdowns where smart moves beat everyone since nothing's hidden.
pros: Replays teach deeper strategies over time.
cons: Top players dominate repeats, boring others.

pairs.tendency: Players talk a lot to share plans and help everyone win together against the game.
pros: Builds team trust through open deals on resources.
Encourages creative problem-solving as a group.
cons: Talking can slow the game if players argue.
One quiet player might feel left out.

pairs.tendency: Deals happen right before fights, mixing talk with attacks to steal advantages.
pros: Makes battles exciting with last-second alliances.
Rewards smart talkers who bluff well.
cons: Deals can break trust and cause hard feelings.

pairs.tendency: You risk big moves to speed ahead, but one bad roll sends you back to the start.
pros: Fast games with high replay excitement.
cons: Luck can make leaders unbeatable early.

pairs.tendency: Everyone places workers together to beat a shared challenge like a disaster.
pros: Teaches shared strategy without cutthroat blocking.
Balances roles for fair team contributions.
cons: Long turns make it feel slow.

exemplars_removed.reason: BoardGameGeek full tags (https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/30549): worker-placement absent

pairs.tendency: Players pass and play cards from hands to chain combos against the game.
pros: Deep planning with card trades feels united.
High skill ceiling for expert teams.
cons: Bad draws doom the whole group.
Analysis paralysis from too many options.

pairs.tendency: You read opponents' plays to win tricks, with little luck in card deals.
pros: Rewards memory and prediction over chance.
Tight games where skill shines through.

triads.tendency: Players race ahead by risking big moves but often smash into each other, causing chaotic fights that slow everyone down.
pros: Creates thrilling high-stakes chases with sudden betrayals.
Heightens tension as risks amplify rival attacks.
cons: Frustration from lost progress due to bad luck or blocks.
Can feel unfair when confrontation halts races unpredictably.

triads.tendency: Everyone sees the board and plans worker spots to grab the best spots for victory points, leading to careful blocking and optimization.
pros: Promotes smart long-term planning with visible competition.
cons: Can cause analysis paralysis from overthinking options.
Early blocks snowball into runaway leads.

triads.tendency: Teammates hide cards while working together to survive threats, creating doubt about who can be trusted even without traitors.
pros: Builds suspense through partial secrecy in teamwork.
cons: Hidden info frustrates coordination in crises.
Misplays from poor info sharing lead to quick losses.

triads.tendency: Friends secretly include a betrayer who sabotages while pretending to help, blending teamwork with hidden backstabbing.
cons: Traitor wins feel random if not spotted early.

triads.tendency: Fighters claim territories through brutal clashes until only one dominates the map as the survivor.
pros: Epic battles for map dominance feel visceral.
cons: Player elimination drags out multi-hour games.

triads.tendency: Players pick cards in turns to build matching sets that score big points, denying rivals key combos.
pros: Quick, elegant card selection with combo potential.
Scalable depth for varied player counts.
cons: Drafting order luck influences set quality.
Weak sets lead to inevitable low scores.

triads.tendency: Roll dice to dash to the end, but random paths and events make it a wild luck fest with little control.
pros: Simple, fast family fun with no deep strategy.
Pure chance evens odds for casual play.
cons: Feels pointless as skill doesn't matter.
Long streaks of bad rolls ruin races.

triads.tendency: Place tiles to connect features for points while everyone sees and blocks your best layouts.
cons: Table space explodes with large maps.

triads.tendency: Secret hands fuel surprise attacks, forcing players to bluff strength while timing card plays.
pros: Bluffing adds mind games to combat.
Hand limits create tough discard choices.
cons: Stale hands lead to predictable plays.

triads.tendency: Guess who's the secret betrayer by piecing together clues and actions amid hidden roles.
pros: Intense whodunit reveals with logic layers.

triads.tendency: Secret bids from hands compete for point-rich assets, bluffing value to outmaneuver rivals.
pros: Hidden bids enable clever bluffs for steals.
cons: Bad hands force weak bids consistently.

triads.tendency: Partners secretly bid tricks with hidden cards, coordinating wins without direct talk.

pros: Diplomacy adds flavor to territorial wars.

triads.tendency: Team risks collective pushes against disasters, banking shared rewards or busting together.
cons: One bad push wipes team progress.

feeling_blocks.description: Loud table, big swings, you can't look away.
Your choices matter, you feel smart.
Laughing at what just happened, absurd moments.
You're on edge, something could go wrong any moment.
You and your friends are in it as one. Shared fate.
Hiding things, tricking people, secret plans.
The dice or the draw felt magical. You got away with it.
You're directing something. Deep decisions have weight.

feeling_blocks.exemplar: Betrayal at House on the Hill

feeling_blocks.description: You sit back and think. Time to plan.
The game moves. Short turns, quick rounds.
Someone got wrecked. Everyone laughed. Including them.
One wrong move and you're in trouble. Precision matters.
You tried something risky and it paid off (or didn't).
Warm. Nobody's out to get anyone.

conflicts.note: Deterministic conflict — a game cannot meaningfully be both solo-in-parallel and directly confrontational. If both selected, flag to the student: 'These two pull against each other — can a game really be both?'

v1_scope_notes.unverified_entries: Items flagged 'perplexity-flagged-check' (7 pairs total) need spot-verification against BGG mechanism tags before workshop use. All others carry 'perplexity-bgg-verified' status from inline RAG during generation.
known_gaps: Theme dimension has no pair entries — theme is treated as orthogonal colour for v1. Re-examine if workshops suggest otherwise.
Many narrower cross-dimensional pairs not generated (e.g. bidding + semi-cooperative, set-collection + team-vs-team). Add as workshops surface specific combinations.
Feeling-block cross-references could be more fine-grained — current supported_by lists 3-5 mechanics, could extend to weight-graded (strong/moderate/weak support).
expected_post_workshop_refinements: Plain-language descriptions simplified further if 12-year-olds hesitate on current phrasing.
Additional feelings added if children reach for words the catalogue doesn't have ('scary', 'romantic', 'weird' are candidates).
Exemplar swaps based on which games children recognise (Indian market may differ from Euro/US BGG bias).
